Gujarat braces for 6 days of heavy rain:4 weather systems turn active: orange alert in 7 districts, including Surat; departments told to remain alert
Red alert in 8 districts including Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat on July 31.
With four rain systems becoming active simultaneously over Gujarat, rainy conditions are set to return from today (30 July). The Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall for the next six days across several parts of the state.
Districts in North Gujarat, Central Gujarat and South Gujarat may witness intense showers. An Orange Alert has been issued for seven districts, including Surat, for July 30.
A Red Alert warning for extremely heavy rainfall has been declared for eight districts, including Ahmedabad, Vadodara and Surat, for July 31.
47 talukas received rainfall
On 29 July, between 6 AM and 8 PM, rainfall was recorded in 47 talukas across the state. The highest rainfall was recorded in Sanjeli of Dahod at 1.38 inches. Singvad in Dahod received 1.06 inches, while Lunawada in Mahisagar recorded around one inch of rainfall.
Due to heavy rainfall in upstream areas of the Dholera region, waterlogging has been reported, with visuals showing water spread across several locations.
Red Alert issued for eight districts on July 31
According to the latest forecast, rainfall intensity is expected to increase in the coming days. Today (30 July), very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in parts of South Gujarat and Central Gujarat.
On 31 July, a Red Alert for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued for Ahmedabad, Anand, Vadodara, Bharuch, Narmada, Surat, Tapi and Dang districts. On August 1, North Gujarat is expected to receive intense rainfall, for which an Orange Alert has been issued.
Weather Watch Group reviews preparedness in Gandhinagar
Amid the possibility of heavy rainfall and monsoon-related challenges, a meeting of the Weather Watch Group was held at the State Emergency Operation Center (SEOC) in Gandhinagar under the chairmanship of Relief Commissioner Gaurang Makwana.
The Relief Commissioner instructed all concerned departments to map their teams and resources and remain prepared for immediate action.
Departments have also been directed to ensure safety measures for people living in dilapidated buildings, remove dangerous hoardings, and issue timely warnings to residents of low-lying areas and temporary structures.
